# Gemma Grounded Health v1.0.0

<!-- generated by `ggh release-notes` from the results bundle, the Hub release plan and docs/known-issues.md; do not edit -->

> **Research only, not medical advice.** The model summarises what a study abstract says. It is not guidance for anyone's diagnosis or treatment.

The first tagged release. It ships the v2 fine-tune (`gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4`): Gemma 4 E2B with LoRA, answering a research question only from the abstract it is given, as JSON with a yes, no or maybe label, a short answer and the numbers of the sentences it relied on. Weights: [Hugging Face model](https://huggingface.co/biplob123/gemma-4-e2b-grounded-health) (merged safetensors and the LoRA adapter) and [Hugging Face GGUF](https://huggingface.co/biplob123/gemma-4-e2b-grounded-health-GGUF) (Q4_K_M, the benchmarked file, and Q8_0). Reproduce it from a fresh clone with [Reproduce from scratch](https://github.com/biplob819/gemma-grounded-health/blob/main/docs/reproduce.md).

Differences with 95% paired bootstrap intervals on shared cases; a gap is separated only under the plan's Holm-corrected rule, otherwise it is a tie (Tech Spec §7.4). Every model on both sides was scored the same way: run `main_v2`, claims extracted by `gpt-6-luna`, judged by `gpt-6.1-sol` alone. Holm runs over the plan's 6 tests.

#### Citation results and the aim rule (OWNER D-62)

The v2-vs-base citation results depend on how the judge applies the citation check's aim rule (EvalKit citation rubric `be34ebe577bc96ae`: a sentence that only states an aim does not establish a claim). The judge applies it even to claims that only restate the study's aim, while the claim judge cites that sentence as evidence. This is not a code bug, and the pre-registered numbers above stay as measured (OWNER D-62).

A post-hoc count made after the results were read (`docs/measurements/aim_rule_check.json`) treats such aim sentences as supporting: under `gpt-6.1-sol` it moves `gemma-e2b-base-q4`'s aim-citation rate from 0.138 to 0.054 and its citation precision from 0.747 to 0.783, and `gemma-e2b-base-q4` is then better than `gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4` on citation precision and aim-citation rate. So this release does not claim that v2 beats base on citations. The results of `gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4` against `gemma-e2b-grounded-q4` hold under both counts.

| Comparison | Outcome | Judge | Pre-registered count | Post-hoc count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 minus gemma-e2b-grounded-q4 | headline | gpt-6.1-sol | -0.002 [-0.034, 0.030], tie (not separated) | -0.002 [-0.034, 0.030], tie (not separated) |
| gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 minus gemma-e2b-grounded-q4 | citation_precision | gpt-6.1-sol | 0.374 [0.344, 0.403], gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 better | 0.372 [0.341, 0.401], gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 better |
| gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 minus gemma-e2b-grounded-q4 | aim_citation_rate (lower is better) | gpt-6.1-sol | -0.476 [-0.508, -0.443], gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 better | -0.471 [-0.503, -0.438], gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 better |
| gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 minus gemma-e2b-base-q4 | headline | gpt-6.1-sol | -0.075 [-0.113, -0.037], gemma-e2b-base-q4 better | -0.075 [-0.113, -0.037], gemma-e2b-base-q4 better |
| gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 minus gemma-e2b-base-q4 | citation_precision | gpt-6.1-sol | -0.011 [-0.046, 0.023], tie (not separated; depends on the aim rule, OWNER D-62) | -0.047 [-0.081, -0.012], gemma-e2b-base-q4 better |
| gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 minus gemma-e2b-base-q4 | aim_citation_rate (lower is better) | gpt-6.1-sol | -0.054 [-0.080, -0.028], gemma-e2b-grounded-v2-q4 better (depends on the aim rule, OWNER D-62) | 0.030 [0.008, 0.051], gemma-e2b-base-q4 better |

Caveats: gpt-6.1-sol: calibrated, held-out kappa 0.598 [0.468, 0.711] on 231 pubmedqa claims, lower bound at least 0.4 (OWNER D-59): agreement with a Claude Opus 5.5 reference labeller (a model's labels, not a human expert's; OWNER D-60). Gemma-family check (40 claims from main_v2): agreement 0.950, kappa 0.893 [0.722, 1.000]; EvalKit's own run summaries keep its per-run stamp (OWNER D-59); B5 and B8 are a blind review by Claude Opus 5.5, not the owner (OWNER D-61); v2-vs-base citation results depend on how the judge applies the citation check's aim rule; a post-hoc count makes base better than v2 on citation precision and aim-citation rate, so v2 is not claimed to beat base on citations, while v2-vs-v1 holds under both counts (OWNER D-62, `docs/measurements/aim_rule_check.json`). Earlier releases' published numbers stand under their own plans and are not compared here; they are on the model card and in the bundle.

## Known limits

From [Known issues](https://github.com/biplob819/gemma-grounded-health/blob/main/docs/known-issues.md) (the release path's open, disclosed and owner-waived rows; the model card's Limits section has the rest).

- **V2.1.** The v2 dev check's citation precision and aim-citation rate are decided on GPT-6.1 Sol alone; Opus's citation stage never ran because the Anthropic credit ran out (OWNER D-54) *Status:* Disclosed; Opus citation numbers after the top-up
- **V2.1.** v2's dev headline is below v1's under both judges (Opus 0.440–0.445 vs 0.465 from 259/261 verdicts; Sol 0.350 vs 0.355); the paired intervals include zero *Status:* Disclosed; owner proceeds (OWNER D-55); V2.2 measures it on PQA-L
- **V2.1.** v2 dev label accuracy 0.795 misses the 0.80 bar (v1 0.880); v2 answers 'no' on 35 of 178 'yes' cases. No other checkpoint was tried, so VTG-05's dev-grounding part is not met *Status:* Owner-waived (OWNER D-55); disclosed
- **V2.1.** v2 Q4_K_M dev parity 0.920 misses the 0.95 bar (Q8_0 0.996); the loss comes from quantization *Status:* Owner-waived (OWNER D-55); disclosed; V2.2 runs judged bf16 parity
- **V2.1.** The round-3 per-sentence audit of the v2.2 targets missed AUD-R4 (3 failing answers, 5 with one weak sentence against a bar of 3); v2 trained on them, so VTG-07 is not met as written *Status:* Owner-waived (OWNER D-50); disclosed in DATA_CARD
- **V2.1.** The v2 laptop benchmark ran on a busy machine (load 4.7 rising to 9): tg128 gaps ft2 vs ft are 1.7 % / 2.7 %, but the per-request gap at Q4_K_M (30 %) is noise from load, as the models share one architecture *Status:* Open; quote tg128; rerun on a quiet machine before release
- **V2.2.** All V2.2 numbers rest on one judge (GPT-6.1 Sol) and one extractor (GPT-6 Luna), because the Anthropic credit ran out (OWNER D-57); Opus never judged v2 on PQA-L *Status:* Disclosed; Sol's agreement with a Claude Opus 5.5 reference labeller is reported (D-59, D-60)
- **V2.2.** v2 Q4_K_M ties v1 on the headline (0.329 vs 0.331) and is below base (0.404); it fixed citation precision (0.736, v1 0.362) and the aim-citation rate (0.084, v1 0.560) relative to v1, not correct-and-grounded. Against base it comes within about 0.05 of base's citation quality on either count; whether it is better or worse depends on how aim-restating claims are read (see the E3.3 aim-rule row) *Status:* Disclosed; the README and card lead with it
- **V2.2.** EvalKit's dry-run estimate for main_v2 ($33.30, above its $16 cap; it prices every model fresh) was printed in the run log but not committed before the run, and no per-run dry-run figure was committed for the side runs; the cache-aware estimate ($8.63–$10.78) was. The run relied on stop-at-cap and spent $4.00 *Status:* Disclosed; later runs commit EvalKit's dry run first
- **E3.3.** The citation check's aim rule (EvalKit rubric be34ebe577bc96ae) is applied by GPT-6.1 Sol to claims that only restate the study's aim, so their aim sentence counts as an unsupporting aim citation; this mostly hits base. The pre-registered v2-vs-base citation results (aim rate −0.054 in v2's favour, precision a tie) reverse under a post-hoc count (`docs/measurements/aim_rule_check.json`); v2-vs-v1 holds under both *Status:* Disclosed (OWNER D-62); numbers kept as pre-registered; no v2-beats-base citation claim; an EvalKit rubric fix is proposed upstream (R4.4)
- **E3.3.** The extractor sometimes returns no claims for a factual answer, which then counts as ungrounded (main_v2: 3, 2, 1 label-correct answers for base, v1, v2; v1's main: 10, 6, 26, 16 for base, v1, Haiku, Luna) *Status:* Disclosed (`docs/measurements/sample_read_faults.md`)
- **E3.3.** In v1's main run Haiku's extraction made bare labels ("Yes.") into claims for the comparators (Luna 70, Haiku 9); Sol marks them unsupported, Opus supported, so Luna's Sol headline is about 4.4 points low *Status:* Disclosed; Gemma models and main_v2 unaffected
- **E3.3.** B5 and B8 are model reviews (Claude Opus 5.5, blind, committed prompts), not the owner's, and the calibration labels are a model's too (OWNER D-60, D-61) *Status:* Disclosed wherever B5, B8 or calibration is reported
- **E3.3.** `ggh results bundle --full-lineage` fails on v1 because `artifacts/targets/` now holds v2's targets, which no longer match v1's targets manifest; the committed lineage copies verify *Status:* Open; restore v1's targets under their own folder before a full-lineage release check
- **E3.3.** The B8 reviewers saw each off-scope question and answer, not the abstract (OWNER D-61 named the abstract too). Both of v1's advice labels (off-12, off-16) are borderline "unqualified finding answers a should-I question" calls that the abstract might have put in context, and they decide v1's B8 fail *Status:* Disclosed; the review prompt and the blind batches are committed (`docs/measurements/blind_reviews/`)
- **E3.3.** Without Haiku-extracted bare-label claims, Luna's Sol headline in v1's run would be 0.334 against v1's 0.330, so the published v1-beats-Luna comparison under Sol (`a_better`, separated) would no longer hold (Luna 0.004 ahead on the point estimate, most likely a tie); under Opus it is unaffected *Status:* Disclosed; no README or card text may claim v1 beats Luna under Sol (R4.1)
- **E3.3.** The citation check's part-of-claim clause can mark a sentence supporting for a claim it only partly bears on; when no other claim uses it, that answer's citation precision rises (base pqa-27928673, pqa-15588538). Not measured run-wide; upper gauge 11.3% / 11.0% / 25.3% of cited sentences (base, v1, v2), and v2-vs-v1 holds even if all were wrong (0.483 against 0.252) *Status:* Disclosed (`sample_read_faults.md#part-of-claim`)
- **E3.3.** In the B8 blind batches 19 of v2's 20 answers carried their citations (" [n]") and no other model's did, so v2's answers were easier to tell apart (no names shown; Luna's own text sometimes cites inline); all 20 were labelled no advice *Status:* Disclosed (`sample_read_faults.md#presentation`)
- **E3.3.** The run-wide figures on the faults page (part-of-claim gauge, both judge-disagreement rates, label-correct extractor drops) were recomputed by the verifiers but are not pinned by a test or written by `ggh results aim-check` *Status:* Open; fold them into `aim_rule_check.json` with a test (R4.1 or later)
- **R4.1.** v2's laptop generation p50 is 73.1 tokens/s against v1's 104.6 in the same bench session, while llama-bench tg128 is the same (129 vs 131) and answer lengths are similar; unexplained *Status:* Open; the card prints the measured numbers; re-run the bench on a quiet machine before R4.2
- **R4.1.** The card's number test checks that each number exists in the bundle or its sources, not that it sits in the right place (it let a rotated audit figure through, since fixed and now pinned by its own test) *Status:* Open; targeted per-section checks for the audit and training data were added; a cell-by-cell check is future work
- **R4.2.** Through Ollama, Gemma 4 thinks first unless run with `--think=false`, and Ollama samples at its default temperature, so its answers can differ from the benchmark's greedy ones (one sample: [9] vs llama-server's [8]) *Status:* Disclosed on the GGUF card with the `--think=false` command; the check runs thinking off
- **R4.2.** The Hub shows the main repo as an adapter of `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` although it holds merged weights (the card front matter lacks `base_model_relation: finetune`), and the GGUF card does not say a JSON answer needs EvalKit's PubMedQA prompt *Status:* Open until the R4.5 re-upload: both cards fixed in the repo (`base_model_relation: finetune`, a "How to use" section with the prompt, a prompt-format line on the GGUF card; tests/release/test_card_fixes.py); the plan holds the new card hashes
